observations: Photo 0 shows the Battery Health & Charging screen of an iPhone, indicating 64% maximum capacity and a degraded battery message.
Photo 1 shows the 'About' section of the iPhone settings, clearly displaying 'Model Name: iPhone 12 Pro Max', 'Model Number: MG9R3LL/A', and 'Capacity: 128 GB'.
Photo 2 shows the lock screen of the iPhone with a wallpaper of a person in front of a car, time 10:22, date Saturday 31 October, and battery at 32%.
All photos show the phone being held in hand, with no visible damage to the front screen or back in these shots.
The seller claims a faulty front camera, cracked back, and no Face ID.

claims.evidence: Photo 1 screen clearly shows 'Model Name: iPhone 12 Pro Max'.

claims.evidence: No photo shows the front camera in use or any visible damage. No video or test shot is provided.
No photo shows the back of the phone. The back is not visible in any of the three photos.
Face ID functionality cannot be verified from photos alone. No test of Face ID is shown.

risks.proof: A video showing battery drain over time or a test of battery life under load.
risks.if_unproven: priced as degraded battery, with reduced value

Video or photo showing the front camera in use to verify functionality.

response.reason: The model is clearly identified as iPhone 12 Pro Max, but critical claims about the front camera, back crack, and Face ID cannot be verified from the current photos. These unverified issues directly affect the value and usability of the phone. Without proof, the item cannot be priced accurately.
